a.text: “Yes, — the bad into the crop, the good into the pot.”

b.text: "Yes, — the bad ones into the little crop, the good ones into the little pot."

a.text: Highly esteemed friend!

b.text: Highly esteemed friend!

a.text: Never have I heard your so highly excellent son so magnificent and incomparable as yesterday in Meyerbeer's immortal work, although he is always the first tenor of the present day. My joy was doubled when I caught sight of his so highly revered and likewise incomparable father among the audience, and told myself what he must be feeling at that moment!

b.text: Never have I heard your so most excellent son as gloriously and incomparably as yesterday in Meyerbeer's immortal work, although he is always the foremost tenor of the present day. My joy was doubled when I caught sight of his so highly honoured and likewise incomparable father among the listeners, and told myself what he must be feeling there!

a.text: Yet to my late, great friend, alas, the good fortune was not granted to hear his Raoul thus!

b.text: But my departed great friend, alas, was not granted the good fortune of hearing his Raoul sung in this way!

a.text: May God preserve you!

b.text: God keep you!

a.text: Your faithfully devoted Carl Kaskel, on 30th June 1864

b.text: Your faithfully devoted, on the 30th of June, Carl Kaskel, 1864

google/gemini-3.8-flash.translation: Highly esteemed friend!
Never have I heard your so highly excellent son so magnificent and incomparable as yesterday in Meyerbeer's immortal work, although he is always the first tenor of the present day.
My joy was doubled when I caught sight of his so highly revered and likewise incomparable father among the audience, and told myself what he must be feeling at that moment!
Yet to my late, great friend, alas, the good fortune was not granted to hear his Raoul thus!
May God preserve you!
Your faithfully devoted Carl Kaskel, on 30th June 1864

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5.translation: Highly esteemed friend!

Never have I heard your so most excellent son as gloriously and incomparably as yesterday in Meyerbeer's immortal work, although he is always the foremost tenor of the present day. My joy was doubled when I caught sight of his so highly honoured and likewise incomparable father among the listeners, and told myself what he must be feeling there!
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5.note: The sentence-final 'müßte' is as transcribed; the sentence ends with an exclamation mark.

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5.translation: But my departed great friend, alas, was not granted the good fortune of hearing his Raoul sung in this way!
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5.note: 'seinen Raoul' refers to the role of Raoul in Meyerbeer's work; 'meinem verewigten großen Freunde' presumably refers to Meyerbeer.

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5.translation: God keep you!
Your faithfully devoted, on the 30th of June, Carl Kaskel, 1864

a.text: A fresh, fragrant breeze billows in the grove by the starlight, and Philomel's night-song echoes; the shepherdess, alas! perceives it not.

b.text: A fresh fragrant rustling wafts in the grove by the light of the stars, and Philomel's night-song resounds; the shepherdess, alas! does not hear it.

a.text: Angered, the elves are seen wandering, that desire breaks the flower of chastity; laments are heard echoing in the grove; the shepherdess, alas! perceives them not.

b.text: One sees the elves drift about in anger, because pleasure breaks the flower of chastity; one hears laments echo in the grove; the shepherdess, alas! does not hear them.

a.text: Yet at last, in the shimmer of the moon, she was seen upon the shepherd's arm: the elves' funerary wailing sounds where they walk intoxicated in the valley.

b.text: But at last she was seen in the shimmer of the moon on the shepherd's arm: the elves' grave-whimpering sounds where, intoxicated, she walks in the valley.

a.text: Her purple girdle flutters in the wind, her eye swims in moist radiance; she sighs, 'O! sweet shepherd, where do I now find the lily-wreath of innocence?'

b.text: Her purple girdle flutters in the wind, her eye swims in moist radiance; she sighs, "Oh! sweet shepherd, where shall I now find the lily-wreath of innocence?"

a.text: 'Among crowns that adorn corpses,' thus it whimpers in the misty valley;

b.text: By crowns that adorn corpses, so it whimpers in the misty valley;
